title: Tunnawiya’s Ritual of the River

dating.label: attested c. 14th–13th c. BCE
dating.note: KUB 7.53+ is catalogued as a New Hittite manuscript. The script date is broad and does not fix the date when the ritual was first composed.

purpose: A purification rite for a man or woman troubled by impurity; the text also names repeated child loss and ends with requests for descendants.
attribution: Attributed to Tunnawiya, the Old Woman

phases.name: At the river
phases.idea: Offerings and clay are taken from the riverbank and spring.

phases.name: The cleansing
phases.idea: Animals, figures, textiles and washing act on the patient.

phases.name: Carrying away
phases.idea: Used objects leave by river and fire before the patient passes a gate.

phases.name: Restoration
phases.idea: The cow, fruit tree and Sun-god frame requests for fertility.

steps.title: Bring the black animals
steps.shortDescription: A black sheep, piglet and puppy are prepared; the prescribed sexes depend on the patient.
steps.summary: A black sheep, piglet and puppy are prepared; the prescribed sexes depend on the patient.
steps.evidence: The sheep, piglet and puppy are specified in KUB 7.53+ obv. I 11–16. The black sheep is a ram for a male patient and a ewe for a female patient.

image.note: The tablet distinguishes a black ram for a man and a black ewe for a woman; the illustration shows one ewe. The piglet and puppy also change sex with the patient.

steps.title: Set out the black clothes
steps.shortDescription: Black clothing, shoes and wool are supplied for the patient.
steps.summary: Black clothing, shoes and wool are supplied for the patient.

image.note: The opening supply list names a black shirt, leggings, wool and shoes; the image groups the garments before the patient puts them on.

steps.title: Offer bread and wine at the riverbank
steps.shortDescription: Thin bread, groats and wine are placed and poured for the riverbank Mother-goddess.
steps.summary: Thin bread, groats and wine are placed and poured for the riverbank Mother-goddess.

image.note: The image groups the thin bread, groats and wine that Tunnawiya brings to the riverbank.

steps.title: Address the riverbank Mother-goddess
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya asks the riverbank Mother-goddess to cleanse the patient with clay.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya asks the riverbank Mother-goddess to cleanse the patient with clay.

image.note: Riverbank clay accompanies the appeal. The female relief is an iconographic comparison, not an identified portrait of this Mother-goddess.

steps.title: Take clay from the riverbank
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya takes clay from the riverbank after the appeal.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya takes clay from the riverbank after the appeal.

image.note: Moist clay stands for the material Tunnawiya takes from the riverbank after addressing its Mother-goddess.

steps.title: Offer bread and wine at the spring
steps.shortDescription: Thin bread, groats and wine are offered at the spring.
steps.summary: Thin bread, groats and wine are offered at the spring.

image.note: The bread and wine cutout is shared with the riverbank offering; this second offering takes place at a spring.

steps.title: Take clay from the spring
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya takes clay from the spring after asking it to draw impurity out.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya takes clay from the spring after asking it to draw impurity out.

image.note: The clay cutout is shared with the riverbank collection; the spring is the second place named for taking clay.

steps.title: Build the reed shelter
steps.shortDescription: A reed shelter is built beside the river, away from tilled land.
steps.summary: A reed shelter is built beside the river, away from tilled land.

image.note: The source requires a reed shelter near a river and away from ploughing; the precise frame and roof shape are illustrative.

steps.title: Make clay tongues and oxen
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya models twelve tongue shapes and two oxen from the collected clay.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya models twelve tongue shapes and two oxen from the collected clay.

image.note: The tablet names twelve clay tongues and two clay oxen. Their exact forms are not preserved; the icon shows all twelve tongues.

steps.title: Dress the patient in black
steps.shortDescription: At first light the patient puts on the black clothes.
steps.summary: At first light the patient puts on the black clothes.

image.note: The black shirt and leggings come from the opening supply list; here the patient puts them on.

steps.title: Hold a black sheep over the patient
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya holds a black sheep over the patient while reciting.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya holds a black sheep over the patient while reciting.
steps.evidence: KUB 7.53+ Vs. I 32′–Vs. I 35′. This passage is partly restored in the surviving text.

image.note: The hands and posture are reconstructed; the tablet specifies lifting the black sheep over the patient.

steps.title: Hold the piglet over the patient
steps.shortDescription: A piglet is held over the patient with its own incantation.
steps.summary: A piglet is held over the patient with its own incantation.
steps.evidence: KUB 7.53+ Vs. I 36′–Vs. I 38′. This passage is partly restored in the surviving text.

image.alt: A piglet lifted above the patient
image.note: The named action is depicted; clothing and implement forms are illustrative.

steps.title: Hold the puppy over the patient
steps.shortDescription: A puppy is held over the patient with its own incantation.
steps.summary: A puppy is held over the patient with its own incantation.
steps.evidence: KUB 7.53+ Vs. I 36′–Vs. I 38′. This passage is partly restored in the surviving text.

image.alt: A puppy lifted above the patient
image.note: The named action is depicted; clothing and implement forms are illustrative.

steps.title: Hold a clay tongue over the patient
steps.shortDescription: A clay tongue is lifted over the patient with a prescribed incantation.
steps.summary: A clay tongue is lifted over the patient with a prescribed incantation.
steps.evidence: KUB 7.53+ Vs. I 39′–Vs. II 7. This passage is partly restored in the surviving text.

image.note: The named object is shown; the exact gesture is described in the step text.

steps.title: Melt the wax and tallow figures
steps.shortDescription: After holding the figures over the patient, Tunnawiya melts them.
steps.summary: After holding the figures over the patient, Tunnawiya melts them.
steps.evidence: KUB 7.53+ Vs. II 14–Vs. II 20. This passage is partly restored in the surviving text.

image.note: The text names wax and tallow figures. Their shapes and the exact melting setup are illustrative.

steps.title: Wash the hands with wine
steps.shortDescription: The patient rises and washes the hands with wine.
steps.summary: The patient rises and washes the hands with wine.

image.note: The patient rises and washes the hands with wine; the jug and basin are shown to isolate that action.

steps.title: Wash oneself with water
steps.shortDescription: The patient washes with water while Tunnawiya continues the incantation.
steps.summary: The patient washes with water while Tunnawiya continues the incantation.

image.note: The tablet does not identify a body part or vessel; an arm and jug stand for the washing.

steps.title: Take blue and red wool off the patient
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya removes blue and red wool from the patient while speaking.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya removes blue and red wool from the patient while speaking.

image.alt: Blue and red wool pulled away.
image.note: The tablet names the colours and removal; the textile placement and hands are reconstructed.

steps.title: Slit the black shirt
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya cuts the black shirt down its length and removes the dark garments.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya cuts the black shirt down its length and removes the dark garments.

image.note: The named object is shown; the exact gesture is described in the step text.

steps.title: Smash the empty pot
steps.shortDescription: An empty pot is waved over the patient and smashed.
steps.summary: An empty pot is waved over the patient and smashed.

image.note: The vessel form is illustrative; the tablet specifies that it is empty and broken.

steps.title: Bathe over a clay figure
steps.shortDescription: A clay figure is placed beneath the patient’s feet as the patient bathes.
steps.summary: A clay figure is placed beneath the patient’s feet as the patient bathes.

image.note: The named object is shown; the exact gesture is described in the step text.

steps.title: Comb the patient downward
steps.shortDescription: Maidservants draw boxwood combs downward over the patient.
steps.summary: Maidservants draw boxwood combs downward over the patient.

image.note: The named object is shown; the exact gesture is described in the step text.

steps.title: Send the used objects into the river
steps.shortDescription: The combs, clothing and other used objects are sent into the river.
steps.summary: The combs, clothing and other used objects are sent into the river.

image.note: The image shows a small group entering water; the tablet lists further objects and does not specify how each entered the river.

steps.title: Burn the piglet and puppy
steps.shortDescription: The puppy and piglet are taken to uncultivated ground and burned.
steps.summary: The puppy and piglet are taken to uncultivated ground and burned.

image.note: The burning is explicit. The size of the fire and position of the animals are reconstructed.

steps.title: Pass beneath the wooden gate
steps.shortDescription: The patient leaves beneath the alanza-wood gate as Tunnawiya speaks.
steps.summary: The patient leaves beneath the alanza-wood gate as Tunnawiya speaks.

image.note: The source names alanza wood and a temporary gate. Its construction and botanical species are not securely known.

steps.title: Offer bread again at the riverbank
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya returns to the riverbank with bread and groats.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya returns to the riverbank with bread and groats.

image.note: This return offering names bread and groats; wine is libated in the following passage. The shared image shows the complete offering set.

steps.title: Take the cow by its horn
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya takes hold of a cow by its horn to begin a fertility comparison.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya takes hold of a cow by its horn to begin a fertility comparison.

image.note: The cow’s breed, colour and horns are illustrative. The source calls it fertile, with a question mark in the draft translation.

steps.title: Ask for offspring through the cow analogy
steps.shortDescription: Addressing the Sun-god, Tunnawiya likens the patient’s hoped-for descendants to a fertile cow’s increase.
steps.summary: Addressing the Sun-god, Tunnawiya likens the patient’s hoped-for descendants to a fertile cow’s increase.

image.note: The animal is the explicit image in the analogy; its coat and breed are illustrative.

steps.title: Take hold of a fruit-bearing tree
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya takes hold of a fruit-bearing tree.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya takes hold of a fruit-bearing tree.

image.note: The source does not identify the tree species. The small red fruit in the image is illustrative, not a botanical identification.

steps.title: Ask for descendants through the tree analogy
steps.shortDescription: Tunnawiya addresses the Sun-god and compares descendants to the fruit on a tree.
steps.summary: Tunnawiya addresses the Sun-god and compares descendants to the fruit on a tree.

image.note: The named object is shown; the exact gesture is described in the step text.

steps.title: Pour wine for the Sun-god
steps.shortDescription: The patient pours a libation and calls on the Sun-god to keep the cleansing effective.
steps.summary: The patient pours a libation and calls on the Sun-god to keep the cleansing effective.

image.note: The named action is depicted; clothing and implement forms are illustrative.
